'''Dean Daniel Oliver''' (born November 5, 1978) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player and assistant coach for the [[Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball|Wisconsin Badgers]]. An [[NBA draft|undrafted]] {{convert|5|ft|11|in|m|adj=on}} [[point guard]] from the [[University of Iowa]], Oliver played with the [[Golden State Warriors]] from [[2001-02 NBA season|2001-02]] to [[2002-03 NBA season|2002-03]].

==Early life and college==
Born in [[Quincy, Illinois]], Oliver graduated from Mason City High School in [[Mason City, Iowa]] in 1997 as a member of the [[National Honor Society]] with a 3.9 GPA.<ref name="NBA bio">{{cite web|title=Dean Oliver bio|url=http://www.nba.com/playerfile/dean_oliver/bio.html|publisher=NBA|accessdate=April 7, 2012}}</ref> At the [[University of Iowa]], Oliver played in the [[Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball|Hawkeyes]] basketball team all four years and graduated in 2001 with a [[Bachelor of Business Administration]] in [[finance]].<ref>[http://www.linkedin.com/in/deanoliver20 Linkedin]</ref> In his senior season, Oliver averaged 14.9 points, 2.8 rebounds, and 4.8 assists per game.<ref name="bb ref"/> Oliver was a three-time third-team All-[[Big Ten Conference]] selection (1999–2001) and led the conference in assist/turnover ratio in his senior season.<ref name="NBA bio"/>

==Professional career==

===Player===
In March 1996 and 1997 Oliver and his fellow players lead his team, the Mason City Mohawks, to two state tournament wins. Head coach at the time was Robert Horner, father of player and future Hawkeye, [[Jeff Horner]]. Oliver was not drafted in the [[2001 NBA draft]] but played two seasons with the [[Golden State Warriors]], who waived Oliver on December 5, 2002. With the Warriors, Oliver played a mostly backup role in 35 games, averaging 1.8 points, 0.7 rebounds, and 1.3 assists per game.<ref name="bb ref">{{cite web|title=Dean Oliver|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/o/olivede01.html|publisher=basketball-reference.com|accessdate=April 7, 2012}}</ref>

Oliver's final NBA game was played on December 3, 2002, in a 110–89 win over the [[Denver Nuggets]] where he recorded 5 points and 1 rebound.

On February 3, 2003, he signed with the [[Greenville Groove]] of the [[NBA Development League]] (D-League). The Groove waived Oliver on February 23, and Oliver signed with the D-League team [[Asheville Altitude]] two days later.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/transactions_0203.html |title=2002-03 Transactions |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=April 8, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120211063257/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/transactions_0203.html |archive-date=February 11, 2012 |url-status=dead }}</ref> In October 2003, Oliver signed with the expansion team of the [[USBL]], Cedar Rapids River Raiders, in his home state of Iowa; the River Raiders would begin play in the spring of 2004.<ref>{{cite web|title=Cedar Rapids pro team signs ex-Hawkeye Oliver|url=http://qconline.com/archives/qco/print_display.php?id=170907|publisher=AP|accessdate=April 7, 2012}}</ref> He then signed with the [[Dakota Wizards]] of the [[Continental Basketball Association|CBA]] in February 2004.<ref>[http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/?id=3000297 Oliver to Suit up for River Raiders Coach in Dakota]</ref> The Wizards won the 2004 CBA title, and Oliver was a backup for the Wizards.<ref name="Globe Gazette 2004">{{cite news|last=Suhr|first=Jamie|title=Oliver hopes road back to NBA begins in Cedar Rapids|url=http://globegazette.com/sports/article_9789f8dc-4b89-533d-bc32-e3998f409752.html|accessdate=April 7, 2012|newspaper=Mason City Globe Gazette|date=May 9, 2004}}</ref>

Oliver began playing in European leagues in 2004.

With [[Śląsk Wrocław (basketball)|Śląsk Wrocław]] of the [[Polish Basketball League]], Oliver scored 17 points to bring the team to third place in the tournament.<ref>{{cite web| url = http://www.eurobasket.com/reports/2007/5/29.asp| url-status = dead| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20081025095407/http://www.eurobasket.com/reports/2007/5/29.asp| archive-date = 2008-10-25| title = Eurobasket Daily News Report: 5/29/2007}}</ref>

From 2007 to 2010, Oliver played for the Dutch team [[EiffelTowers Den Bosch|EiffelTowers]], which won [[Dutch Basketball League]] Cups in 2008<ref>{{cite web| url = http://www.eurobasket.com/reports/2008/4/1.asp| url-status = dead| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20120627045148/http://www.eurobasket.com/reports/2008/4/1.asp| archive-date = 2012-06-27| title = Eurobasket Daily News Report}}</ref> and 2009.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/other-leagues/1194/dutch-cup-for-eiffel-towers-den-bosch.html|title = Sportsglory | Product Guides for Athletes & Sports Records}}</ref>

===Coach===
In 2011, he became the head of basketball operations at North Dakota.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://thegazette.com/2011/09/21/ex-hawkeye-dean-oliver-new-asst-coach-at-north-dakota/|title=Ex-Hawkeye Dean Oliver new asst. Coach at North Dakota}}</ref> In 2014, he became an assistant basketball coach at Illinois State.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.goredbirds.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/051514aaa.html |title=Oliver Hired as Illinois State Men's Basketball Assistant Coach - Illinois State University Official Athletic Site |access-date=May 15, 2014 |archive-date=May 17, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140517151427/http://www.goredbirds.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/051514aaa.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> On April 20, 2017, Oliver was named an assistant at [[Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball|Wisconsin]] under coach [[Greg Gard]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Former Iowa guard Dean Oliver joins Wisconsin basketball staff |url=http://www.thegazette.com/subject/sports/college/mens-basketball/former-iowa-guard-dean-oliver-joins-wisconsin-basketball-staff-20170420|accessdate=April 22, 2017|work=[[Cedar Rapids Gazette]]|date=April 20, 2017}}</ref>
